Do you still remember the feeling of reversing out of your parents' driveway for the first time? That feeling is pure freedom. But for your parents, that moment might be one of the most terrifying moments of their lives. When you were a teenager, your parents had absolutely no way of knowing whether you were speeding, where you went, when you arrived, or how safely you were driving. No news was good news, and hope was the only tool available at the time, until you called to report safe arrival.

If you currently have a teenager who is driving, you should be grateful that nowadays you no longer have to endure the unknown fear that generation of parents went through. Technology in 2026 has plenty of downsides, but HeyPolo is a perfect example of how technology can make the lives of teen drivers better and safer.

HeyPolo is more than just a paid version of Apple's 'Find My' service.

HeyPolo is a family safety app, and one price already includes real-time location sharing, arrival and departure notifications, SOS emergency alerts, as well as driving safety features. The driving features are exactly what sets it apart from regular location-sharing apps (such as Apple's 'Find My'). Every single driving trip your teen driver takes will be recorded and scored, so you can clearly see the details of the trip: their speed, whether they used their phone while driving, whether there was hard braking or sudden acceleration, and whether any serious driving incidents were detected.

The 'Driving Score' rates every trip based on actual driving behaviour, so you no longer need to guess whether your son or daughter is really driving safely. You can see the data, and if their performance isn't great, you can have a serious talk with them. As their habits improve, you'll see the score gradually go up. Compared to anything available to any previous generation, this is a more practical way to help new drivers improve their driving skills.

Crash detection, arrival alerts, and more practical features

HeyPolo automatically detects crashes and notifies you. Combined with arrival alerts, whether your child is going to school, to sports practice, hanging out with friends, or coming home, you can move from simply hoping 'no news is good news' to actually knowing whether they are safe. You no longer have to wait for them to text or call you after they arrive; you'll know the moment they arrive, and this peace of mind for parents is truly priceless. HeyPolo updates every 5 seconds, so your location information is always accurate.

One price, for the whole family

One HeyPolo subscription can cover your entire family, absolutely no extra per-person charges. It works well whether you use iPhone or Android, so it's no problem if your household has a mix of devices. HeyPolo is developed by the team behind Surfshark, which means they have a very solid privacy infrastructure backing them up. They won't sell your data, you can control who you share with and how much, and when to stop sharing, with all data deleted every 7 days. For a location-centric app, this is very important in terms of privacy.

HeyPolo offers a 30-day money-back guarantee. If you and your family try it and feel it's not right for you, there are also no lock-in contracts, so there's absolutely no reason not to give it a try.

There's also an exclusive offer for 9to5Mac readers, don't miss it

If you're still not tempted by now, let us make the offer even more attractive! Through the link below, 9to5Mac readers can subscribe to HeyPolo at 33% off, meaning the monthly fee for the whole family is only US$3.99 per year. You just need to download the app, create your family group, and then invite family members to join. Setting up HeyPolo only takes a few minutes.

You really don't want to miss this offer. With HeyPolo, you can know how your children are driving, and you'll also know when they arrive. The exclusive offer for 9to5Mac readers not only gives you 33% off HeyPolo, but also includes a 30-day money-back guarantee.
